Get and adjust the stop-word list

Source: R/topics.R
stop_words.Rd

stop_words() returns the built-in English list of stop words, extended with add or reduced with remove. Stop words are frequent function words, such as articles, pronouns, and prepositions, that occur in texts of every topic and so say little about what distinguishes one topic from another; excluding them lets the terms that describe a topic be its content words.

Adding words that every text of a corpus shares, such as the name of the course or the disease a corpus is about, removes them from the topic terms as well. The list filters only the terms and keyword candidates; the text that is embedded is unchanged.

The result is passed as stop_words = to topics(), compare_topics(), topic_corpus(), terms(), or keywords(). A character vector of one's own replaces the list, and character() turns the filter off.

Usage

stop_words(language = "en", add = NULL, remove = NULL)

Arguments

language

Language of the list. Only "en" (default) is available.

add

Words to add to the list, matched case-insensitively. Default NULL.

remove

Words to remove from the list. Default NULL.

Value

A character vector of lower-case stop words, sorted.

Conditions

An error of class sbert_bad_input when language is not "en".

See also

topics() and terms(), which use the list; clean_corpus() to clean the text itself.

Examples

head(stop_words())
#> [1] "a"       "about"   "after"   "again"   "against" "all"    

# Keep the defaults, add two domain words, and drop one entry
custom <- stop_words(add = c("try", "again"), remove = "against")

corpus <- head(dedupe(feedback_translations, column = "translation"), 600)
topic_model <- topics(corpus, n_topics = 6, column = "translation",
                      embeddings = feedback_embeddings, stop_words = custom)
terms(topic_model, n = 3)
